messages:
alex: Anyone else seeing p95 spikes between GPU nodes during the 18:00 batching window? cluster-gpu-3 racks A/B. p95 jumps from ~6ms to 65ms for ~3-5min. :eyes:
jamie: Yep, saw alerts. Correlated with heavy batch ramp for llama-7b on shard group 12.
kai: Packet loss up ~0.2-0.5% on peerlink between host-3a-02 and host-3b-07 during the window.
maria: Ran a quick `mtr` and pings — intermittent latency microbursts, looks like east-west only, north-south still fine.
alex: sharing tcp stats from one host (snip):
```
# ethtool -S enp1s0f0 | egrep "drop|rx_err|tx_err|tx_fifo|rx_miss"
rx_missed_errors: 72
tx_fifo_errors: 0
rx_crc_errors: 0
rx_no_buffer_count: 14
```
jamie: enp1s0f0 also shows increasing rx_missed during the window. Could be interrupt coalescing or buffer exhaustion.
ashley: Are these hosts doing RDMA? I know some jobs use gpudirect on those racks.
kai: We have ib0 up for the cluster but most model traffic goes over TCP/ROCE fallback — some flows use RDMA when available.
maria: Quick check of MTU: hosts report 9000, but TOR shows 1500 on a couple of ports for rack B. Possible jumbo mismatch?
alex: yes — TOR port flaps flagged for host-3b-07 around 18:02, see switch log: "port 17: MTU change from 9000 to 1500"
jamie: That would cause fragmentation and CPU overhead on RX side, causing jitter.
ashley: Can we temporarily pin heavy batches to rack A while we investigate? Risk is capacity reduction but keep latency stable.
alex: I'll push a short routing rule to prefer hosts in rack A for the next 30m and scale down shard group 12 on rack B.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1189 - east-west microburst latency — assigned to eng-infra.
kai: Also seeing some kswapd churn on host-3b-07, maybe kernel reclaim interacting with NIC driver.
maria: Suggest collecting `tcpdump -n -i enp1s0f0 tcp and host <peer>` for one cycle and upload pcap.
jamie: I'll kick off packet capture at 18:05 and post pcap link.
alex: mitigation applied: traffic steering to rack A + lowered batch size for shard 12 by 20% at 18:08. Early metrics show p95 fell back to ~8ms. :thumbsup:
ashley: Good. Next steps: confirm MTU mismatch source (provisioning script or TOR config drift), check RDMA fallback logs, and audit any recent kernel/driver updates.
alex: Assigning to kai to do kernel/driver + NIC firmware check; jamie to own TOR config audit; maria to collect eval logs/pcaps.
kai: On it. Will reimage host-3b-07 if we see driver corruption.
jamie: TOR config diff shows an automated ACL push at 17:50 that touched port configs for rack B — rolling back to baseline now.
ops-bot: Update: rollback completed at 18:22.
maria: pcap uploaded: https://internal-logs.example.com/pcap/2060001111-capture.pcap (snip)
alex: Thanks all. We'll keep the routing rule for 2 hours while we validate. If anyone sees another spike, ping @alex and drop thread.
jamie: FYI cost hit from steering + lower batch size ~+7% on tokens for the hour. Documenting in the incident ticket.
kai: Found NIC stats correlating RX queue drops to softirq spikes; adding irqaffinity tweak to test.
ashley: Good triage. If rollback doesn't hold, escalate to network infra.
alex: Closing initial thread — will update incident with postmortem notes once analysis finishes. :white_check_mark:
